summary: Bernhard Forssman is a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg under Karl Hoffmann (~1956–1964) and held posts at the University of Marburg (1968–1983) and Erlangen-Nuremberg (1983).

Bernhard Geiger worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He earned his Ph.D. at Vienna (1900–1905) under Leopold von Schroeder and studied at Bonn, Göttingen, Charles, and Heidelberg. He taught at Vienna, the Asia Institute, and Columbia.

Bernhard Hirzel was an Indologist who studied at Zurich, Carolinum, Berlin, Göttingen (Ph.D. ~1832–1833), and Paris, learning under Franz Bopp and Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He served at the University of Zurich as reader, docent, and Privatdozent between 1833 and 1845.

Bernhard Jülg was a linguist and Central Asian specialist. He studied at Heidelberg, Berlin under Lachmann, Boeckh, Bopp, Petermann, and Schott, and earned his PhD at Kiel in 1847. He held professorships at Lviv (1851), Jagiellonian (1853), and Innsbruck (1863).

Bernhard Karlgren was a sinologist and linguist. He studied at Uppsala University (~1907–1915), where he also held a post from ~1915 to 1918, before serving at the University of Gothenburg from ~1918 to 1939.

Bernhard Kölver was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. After studying at Kiel, Glasgow, Göttingen, Frankfurt (PhD ~1960–1964 under Werner Thomas), and Cologne, he held posts at Cologne, Kiel (1974–1993), and the University of Leipzig (1993–2001).

Bernie Glassman worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Brooklyn Polytechnic, NYU, and UCLA (Ph.D. ~1964–1970), and trained under Taizan Maezumi and Koryu Osaka. He founded the Zen Center of Los Angeles and Zen Peacemakers (1980).

Bert Vaux is a linguist who earned his BA at the University of Chicago (1986–1990) and MA at Harvard (1990–1994). He has held faculty posts at Harvard (2000–2003), the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee (2003–2006), and the University of Cambridge (2006–present).

Berthe Jansen specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Leiden University (BA 2005–2008, PhD ~2010–2015 under Jonathan A. Silk) and Oxford (MPhil 2008–2010), holding posts at Heidelberg (~2015) and Leiden University (2015–2016).

Berthold Delbrück was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg (Ph.D. ~1859–1863, Habilitation ~1864–1866) under Pott, and under Weber, Bopp, and Steinthal. He served as Privatdozent at Halle-Wittenberg (1867–1870) and professor at the University of Jena (1870–1913).

Berthold Laufer specialized in Sinology, Tibetology, and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berlin and earned his Ph.D. at Leipzig (~1895–1897) under August Conrady. He held positions at the American Museum of Natural History, Columbia, and the Field Museum.
Bertram Fulke Hartshorne was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Charterhouse School (~1858–1863) and completed his B.A. at Pembroke College, Oxford (~1864–1868).

Bertram G. Liyanage works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at Savitribai Phule Pune University (2013–2015), studied at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and became a PhD student at Temple University in 2022.

Beru Khyentse Rinpoche II is a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers including Dzongsar Khenpo Chimey Rinpoche, Kalu Rinpoche, the 16th Karmapa, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

Bettina Bäumer is an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar. She studied at Salzburg, Vienna, Zurich, Rome, Munich (doctorate ~1963–1967), and under Swami Lakshman Joo. She held posts at Banaras Hindu University, Vienna, and the Alice Boner Institute.

Bettine Birge is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. She earned her Ph.D. at Columbia University, studying under Wm. Theodore de Bary, Wing-tsit Chan, and Masaaki Sugiyama, and was a visiting scholar at Academia Sinica in 1994.

Betty Heimann worked in philosophy and Indology. She studied at Heidelberg, Göttingen, Bonn, Kiel (Ph.D. ~1916–1919), Hamburg, and Halle-Wittenberg (Habilitation 1921–1923). She held posts at Halle, Hamburg, SOAS, Oxford, London, and the University of Ceylon (1945–1949).
Betty Jean Shefts is a scholar in linguistics, Tibetology, and Indology. She pursued her studies under Franklin Edgerton, Paul Thieme, and Geshe Nornang.
Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya is a Buddhist studies scholar who has served as Dean at Lumbini Buddhist University and as Chairman of the Lotus Research Centre.

Bhadriraju Krishnamurti was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania (A.M. and Ph.D. ~1954–1957) and under M. B. Emeneau. He held posts at Andhra University, UC Berkeley, Osmania University (1962–1986), and the University of Hyderabad.
